name: project_path_doctor
purpose: Windows PATH auditor that reports dead entries, duplicates and shadowed executables, resolving machine and user PATH in true composition order.
notes: First Rust project on this machine, chosen as a workflow shakedown. Read-only by design: it reports, it never writes PATH. Born from real PATH shadowing hit during machine provisioning on 2026-09-15. Slice 1 is complete - registry reading and composition (winreg, chosen over the windows crate so the unsafe stays in the dependency), per-entry findings, executable enumeration with PATHEXT read from the environment, shadow resolution for both the running process and a fresh one, and the output layer with a versioned JSON contract in docs/SPEC.md. A GUI is a confirmed consumer, so the serialisation shape is defined once in pathdoc-core behind a serde feature rather than mirrored in the front end; it is at schemaVersion 4. Schema 2 replaced a conflicts-only shadows array with a full executables array after three of the four names worth reporting turned out to appear exactly once; schema 3 added live process positions after the tool was found to name the wrong winner for any name present in both a runtime-injected directory and a registry one. Exit 1 is reserved for actionable per-entry findings; shadowing is reported always and gates only under --fail-on-shadow. The acceptance test doubles as a drift canary for the machine's PATH and has caught two unannounced changes; volatile counts are isolated at the top of it. Shell-level masking detection landed at schemaVersion 4: PowerShell aliases and functions that answer to a name before PATH is searched, 24 of them here including sc hiding sc.exe. It extends the per-name executables records rather than being a Finding or a separate section. intercepts is a list and the report names every interpreter consulted, because the verdict is per shell - curl is masked in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and clear in PowerShell 7, verified with --shell powershell --shell pwsh - and because listed-as-consulted is what turns an absent record into asked-and-clear rather than never-asked. Defaults to -NoProfile so the tool never executes user code unasked, and never gates the exit code. Registry access has been extracted into a winenv crate that knows nothing about PATH, so the planned env-var tool depends on it rather than on pathdoc-core: dependencies point from each tool at winenv, never from one tool at another. Decided: winenv stays in this repository, unpublished, and this repository becomes the toolkit workspace with the tools as members when the env-var tool exists - which bends the trunk's one-repo-per-project convention deliberately, for the trunk to amend when the restructure happens. Dual licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 with both licence files present, ready to publish. Tooling entry point is the justfile - just check runs fmt, clippy in both feature configurations, nextest and cargo-deny. GitHub Actions runs the full gate on windows-latest and only fmt-check plus deny on ubuntu-latest, because the workspace cannot build for Linux at all. CI earned its place on its third run by going red on the masking scan: a runner exceeded the ten-second timeout that measures 150 ms here, which exposed three real defects - a timed-out child abandoned rather than killed (nextest reported it as LEAK on a test that passed, and it would have leaked one shell per audit in a long-lived consumer such as the GUI), three portable tests that assumed a live interpreter would answer, and interpreter deduplication running against the ones that had already answered rather than before spawning. Fixed by making the script cheap - Get-Alias plus the Function: drive rather than Get-Command -CommandType Alias,Function, 197 constructs against 1391 with identical results - with the timeout raised to 30 seconds as a hedge rather than a fix. Portable tests now inject a fake shell and spawn nothing; the one real-shell test lives in this_machine.rs and skips loudly. 174 tests. Next is the roadmap: decoding WindowsApps stubs, the env-var backup/diff tool, and an automated shadowing cross-check against Get-Command.
